title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 219 (When agent’s remuneration becomes due)

content.overview: In the absence of any special contract, payment for the performance of any act is not due to the agent until the completion of such act; but an agent may detain moneys received by him on account of goods sold, although the whole of the goods consigned to him for sale may not have been sold, or although the sale may not be actually complete.
content.glance: Absent special contract, remuneration due on completion; agent may detain sale moneys though consignment not fully sold.
content.study: In the absence of any special contract, payment for the performance of any act is not due to the agent until the completion of such act; but an agent may detain moneys received by him on account of goods sold, although the whole of the goods consigned to him for sale may not have been sold, or although the sale may not be actually complete.

sections.heading: Due on completion
sections.body: Absent special contract, payment not due until completion of the act.

sections.heading: Detention of sale moneys
sections.body: Agent may detain moneys received on account of goods sold though consignment not fully sold or sale not complete.

examples.title: Application of Section 219
examples.body: Facts that satisfy the elements stated in the statutory text of Section 219 produce the consequence described in that section. Do not add elements beyond the text.

hypotheticals.question: Do the facts engage Section 219?
hypotheticals.analysis: Compare the facts with the statutory elements in Section 219. If they match, the statutory consequence follows; otherwise it does not.

distinctions.title: Scope of Section 219
distinctions.body: Section 219 applies only to the circumstances described in its statutory text. It does not create additional grounds or remedies beyond those stated.

misconceptions.myth: Section 219 creates unlimited or extra-statutory rights.
misconceptions.correction: Section 219 operates only within the elements and consequences stated in its statutory text.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 219 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Check special contract; otherwise due on completion; note detention of sale moneys.
